transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I came in because after these nights when I eat like that, I just sit there afterward with crumbs and empty containers around me, and I feel so ashamed. Disgusted with myself, really. Sometimes the next morning I can hardly pray, or look people at church in the eye. It’s been bothering me a lot.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or do anything else to try to get rid of the calories or control your weight?
I… I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’ve noticed myself doing anything like that, at least not something I can clearly say. I mostly just feel awful afterward.
When you're eating during these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yes. Once I take that first bite, especially after the house is quiet, it feels like my good sense just steps aside. I’ll be telling myself, “Belinda, stop now,” but my hands keep reaching for more anyway. It’s like I’m not really in control of it then.
How often do these episodes happen where you feel like you can't control your eating once you start?
Since my friend passed, it’s been happening at least once or twice most weeks. I don’t think there’s been a month where it really let up.
Do these episodes of eating make it hard for you to function normally during the day, like at work or with your family?

Yes… it does. I’m not working now, but it’s affecting things I normally do. I’ve started turning down bridge nights and even helping in the church kitchen, because I worry someone will notice missing leftovers or ask why I’m acting so ashamed. It’s embarrassing, so I just stay away.
Do these episodes of eating or the feelings afterward ever make it hard for you to take care of responsibilities at home, like cooking, cleaning, or managing daily tasks?

Yes, it has. I’ve been turning down bridge nights and some of my church kitchen duties because I’m so worried someone will notice missing leftovers or ask why I seem so ashamed. It’s gotten in the way of things I’d normally take care of or show up for.
Do you feel that these eating episodes or the feelings afterward have caused you significant distress in your social life or relationships with others?

Yes, it has. I’ve been pulling away from people. I’ve turned down some bridge nights, and I’ve avoided helping in the church kitchen because I’m afraid someone will notice missing leftovers or ask why I seem so ashamed. It’s made me feel embarrassed and not want to be around others.
Do you often feel guilty or start blaming yourself after these eating episodes, even when you’re alone and no one else is involved?

Yes. After those nights, I’ll sit there with crumbs and empty containers around me, and I just feel so ashamed… disgusted with myself. Even if nobody else knows, I blame myself. The next morning I can hardly pray, or look people at church in the eye.
